# District of Columbia, USA TRAVEL SURVIVAL KIT

**Traveler Types Covered**: Budget/Luxury/Family/Solo/Business

## 1. SIM CARD SOLUTIONS

| **Provider** | **Price Options** | **Data Allocation** | **Validity** | **Where to Buy** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **T-Mobile** | $40 - $60 USD | 10GB to Unlimited | 30 Days | Official stores, major malls |
| **AT&T** | $50 USD | 15GB High Speed | 30 Days | Official stores, Best Buy |
| **Verizon** | $35 - $70 USD | 5GB to Unlimited | 30 Days | Official stores |
| **Airalo (eSIM)** | $4.50 - $26 USD | 1GB to 10GB | 7-30 Days | App Store / Play Store |

**Recommendations**:
*   **Short trips**: Airalo eSIM is the most convenient for data-only needs.
*   **1-4 weeks**: T-Mobile Prepaid plans offer the best balance of price and coverage within the city.
*   **Digital Nomads**: Verizon offers the most robust 5G network if you are traveling outside the city center.

---

## 2. AIRPORT TRANSFERS

**Route**: From Ronald Reagan Washington National (DCA) / Washington Dulles (IAD) to Downtown DC

| **Mode** | **Duration** | **Cost (USD)** | **Booking** | **Best For** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Metro (DCA)** | 15-20 mins | $2.00 - $6.00 | SmarTrip App/Station | Speed, budget |
| **Metro (IAD)** | 55-65 mins | $3.85 - $6.00 | SmarTrip App/Station | Budget (Silver Line) |
| **Ride-hailing** | 20-50 mins | $25 - $70+ | Uber/Lyft App | Door-to-door |
| **Taxi** | 20-50 mins | $20 - $80+ | Curbside | Reliability |

**Details**:
*   **Metro Boarding**: DCA has a station connected via pedestrian bridges. IAD is served by the Silver Line; follow "Metrorail" signs from arrivals.
*   **Frequency**: Trains run every 10-15 minutes depending on the time of day.
*   **Operating Hours**: Mon-Fri 5am-12am, Sat 7am-1am, Sun 7am-12am.

## 3. CURRENCY EXCHANGE

**Current Exchange Rate**: Local Currency is USD ($).

| **Location** | **Why It's Best** | **Address** | **Hours** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **CXI (Currency Exchange Intl)** | Reliable, many currencies | Union Station (Main Hall) | 10am - 6pm |
| **Travelex** | Airport convenience | DCA/IAD Terminals | Flight-dependent |
| **Major Banks** | Best rates for account holders | Various (Chase, Wells Fargo) | 9am - 5pm |

**Universal Tips**:
*   Avoid airport kiosks unless urgent; rates are significantly worse.
*   ATMs (Bank-affiliated) are the most cost-effective way to get cash.
*   DC is highly "cashless"—credit cards are accepted almost everywhere, including food trucks.

## 5. MUST-TRY FOODS

🍽️ **The Half-Smoke** – *Signature Sausage*
*   **What**: A larger, spicier, coarser hot dog, usually grilled and topped with herbs, onion, and chili.
*   **Where**: **Ben’s Chili Bowl** (U Street) is the iconic location.
*   **Price**: $7.00 - $10.00 USD.

🍽️ **Ethiopian Doro Wat** – *Ethnic Staple*
*   **What**: DC has the largest Ethiopian population outside Ethiopia. Spicy chicken stew served on Injera bread.
*   **Where**: **Chercher** or **Dukem** in the Shaw/U Street area.
*   **Price**: $15.00 - $25.00 USD.

🍽️ **Mumbo Sauce** – *Local Condiment*
*   **What**: A sweet, tangy, slightly spicy sauce served over fried chicken or fries.
*   **Where**: Any local "carry-out" Chinese or wing shop (e.g., **Yum's**).
*   **Try with**: Fried chicken wings and fried rice.

## 10. BEST PUBS & BARS

*   **Old Ebbitt Grill**: DC’s oldest saloon. Historic, mahogany-filled, great for oyster happy hour.
*   **The Round Robin Bar**: Located in the Willard Hotel. Famous for the "Mint Julep" and political "people-watching."
*   **Dacha Beer Garden**: (Shaw) Outdoor German-style beer garden, great vibe and pet-friendly.
*   **Service Bar**: (U Street) Incredible cocktails with a casual, unpretentious atmosphere.
*   **VUE at Hotel Washington**: Rooftop bar with the best views of the White House and monuments.

## 11. LOCAL CUSTOMS & ETIQUETTE

Cultural norms in DC revolve around political professionalism and urban efficiency.

### 11a. Temple & Sacred Site Dress Code
Dress codes apply primarily to government buildings and memorials.

| **Rule** | **What to Check** | **Enforcement Level** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Modesty** | Casual is fine, but avoid swimwear at memorials | High (Respect-based) |
| **Headwear** | Remove hats in the Capitol/Museums | Moderate |
| **Footwear** | Comfortable walking shoes are essential | Practicality |

### 11b. The Head, Feet & Body — Cultural Hierarchy
DC follows standard Western social norms.

*   Maintain personal space in lines and on the Metro.
*   Avoid pointing or staring at high-profile individuals or politicians.

### 11c. Professional & Religious Etiquette
Respect for ceremonies and government functions is expected.

| **Rule** | **Detail** | **Who It Applies To** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **National Anthem** | Stand and face the flag | All visitors |
| **Arlington Cemetery**| Maintain silence near the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier | All visitors |
| **Photography** | Prohibited in some museum galleries/security checkpoints | All visitors |

### 11d. Saving Face & Conflict Resolution
Directness is common, but public outbursts are frowned upon in professional areas.

*   Politeness to security personnel (Capitol Police, Secret Service) is mandatory.
*   A quiet, professional approach resolves issues faster than shouting.

### 11e. Responsible Tourism & Civil Discourse
Respect the diverse history and ongoing political activity of the city.

*   Do not leave trash at the National Mall or memorials.
*   Be respectful of protests—they are a daily occurrence and part of the city's fabric.

### 11f. General Social Customs & Greetings
*   **Escalator Etiquette**: Stand on the **RIGHT**, walk on the **LEFT**. This is the most important "unwritten law" in DC.
*   **Tipping**: 18-22% is standard in restaurants; $1-2 per drink at bars.
*   **Business Casual**: The standard dress code for many downtown restaurants.

## 12. SAFETY & PRACTICAL INFORMATION

DC is a major city with varying safety profiles across its quadrants (NW, NE, SW, SE).

### 12a. Vaccinations & Preventative Health
Standard CDC recommendations for the USA apply.

| **Vaccine** | **Priority** | **Notes** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Flu/COVID-19** | Recommended | Seasonal spikes in winter |
| **Tetanus** | Routine | Standard for any urban travel |

### 12b. Seasonal Health Concerns
The DC climate can be extreme and impacts health.

| **Issue** | **Peak Risk** | **Prevention** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Heat Exhaustion**| July - August | High humidity; carry water and use sunscreen |
| **Lyme Disease** | Summer (Wooded areas) | Use DEET in Rock Creek Park or nearby trails |

### 12c. Water & Food Safety
DC has high standards for public health.

| **Source** | **Safety** | **Guidance** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tap water** | Safe | Drinkable throughout the city |
| **Food Trucks** | Safe | Regulated by DC Health Department |

### 12d. Personal Safety & Crime Awareness
While the tourist areas of DC (National Mall, Smithsonian, Georgetown) are heavily policed and generally safe, travelers should remain vigilant.

**ISSUE**: Petty Theft & Pickpocketing
**WHERE IT HAPPENS**: Crowded Metro stations (Gallery Place/Chinatown, L'Enfant Plaza), popular museums, and nightlife hubs like U Street or Adams Morgan.
**HOW IT HAPPENS**: Distraction techniques in crowds or "snatch and grab" of phones from unzipped pockets.
**HOW TO AVOID IT**: Keep your bag zipped and in front of you. Do not leave your phone on the table at outdoor cafes.
**WHAT TO DO**: Contact the Metropolitan Police Department (MPD) or Transit Police if on the Metro.

**ISSUE**: Vehicle Break-ins
**WHERE IT HAPPENS**: Side streets in NE and SE, and even in popular areas like H Street.
**HOW IT HAPPENS**: Smash-and-grab of visible bags, electronics, or loose change.
**HOW TO AVOID IT**: **"Hide your things, lock your car."** Leave absolutely nothing visible in the vehicle.
**WHAT TO DO**: File a police report for insurance purposes; do not confront the perpetrator.

**ISSUE**: Nightlife Safety & Street Awareness
**WHERE IT HAPPENS**: Primarily after midnight in nightlife corridors.
**HOW IT HAPPENS**: Disputes outside clubs or being targeted while intoxicated.
**HOW TO AVOID IT**: Use ride-hailing apps (Uber/Lyft) to go door-to-door at night. Avoid walking alone in poorly lit areas of SE or NE quadrants if unfamiliar with the neighborhood. Stay aware of your surroundings when using your phone near Metro exits.

**ISSUE**: "Monk" and CD Scams
**WHERE IT HAPPENS**: National Mall near the Air & Space Museum or Lincoln Memorial.
**HOW IT HAPPENS**: Individuals dressed as monks hand you a "peace" bracelet or "artists" hand you a CD, then aggressively demand a "donation."
**HOW TO AVOID IT**: Do not take anything handed to you. Keep walking and say "No, thank you."
**WHAT TO DO**: If they become aggressive, move toward a Park Police officer or a crowded museum entrance.

### 12e. Emergency Contacts & Practical Infrastructure

| **Service** | **Contact** | **Notes** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Emergency (Police/Fire/Med)** | 911 | Universal emergency number |
| **Non-Emergency Police** | 311 | For reporting minor crimes |
| **Metropolitan Police** | (202) 727-9099 | Main DC Police line |
| **George Washington Univ Hospital** | (202) 715-4000 | Major hospital in Foggy Bottom |

## 13. SEASONAL CONSIDERATIONS
*   **Cherry Blossom Season (March/April)**: Extremely crowded; book hotels 6 months in advance.
*   **Summer (June-August)**: Very hot and humid; plan outdoor monuments for early morning or evening.
*   **Winter (December-February)**: Can be freezing with occasional snow; museums are a great refuge.

---

## 14. GENERAL TIPS
*   **Free Admission**: Almost all Smithsonian museums and the National Zoo are **free**, though some (like Air & Space or the African American Museum) require timed entry passes booked online in advance.
*   **The DC Circulator**: A red bus that costs only $1.00 (or free during certain periods) and loops around major tourist sites.
*   **Circulating the Mall**: The National Mall is much larger than it looks. Wear comfortable shoes or rent a "Capital Bikeshare" bike to save time.
